title: Arrow Wrangler Package
text:
1 Executive Summary
Arrow Wrangler python package is used to standardise data manipulation with pyarrow datasets

title: data_manipulation
text:
data_manipulation
Pins functions and ArrowWrangler class for helping with arrow data manipulations.





Name
Description




ArrowWrangler
Data Munger using Arrow datasets.





data_manipulation.ArrowWrangler(start_arrow, board=None)
Data Munger using Arrow datasets.


>>> from pins.data import mtcars
>>> mtcars_arrow = pa.table(mtcars)
>>> c = ArrowWrangler(mtcars_arrow)
>>> c.pipe_ibis(lambda d: d.mutate(x=1)).dataframe
>>> c.pipe_pandas(lambda d: d.iloc[:, 1:2])






Name
Description




board
Get board.


dataframe
Get dataframe.









Name
Description




pipe_arrow
Apply a function to the ArrowWrangler object in a chain-able manner.


pipe_ibis
Apply formula taking input ibis table and output ibis table.


pipe_pandas
Apply formula taking input pandas DataFrame and output pandas DataFrame.


pipe_sql
Apply formula using sql via duckdb (tsql dialect).


read_from_board
Read from board and save it to the object instance’s dataframe property.


read_from_sqlserver
Read from sql server database and initialize new ArrowWrangler object.


save_arrow_ifnew
Save arrow table to a board if it is new file (different to latest board pin).


save_excel
Save arrow table to a board if it is new file (different to latest board pin).

required

()


other_datasets
list | None
List of strings defining the names of data pins to read from the board. If this is used, the name of the string needs to be the name of the parameter that the function is passed to. eg if pipe_arrow has other_datasets=[‘cobe’, ‘bp’], then this needs to be the other datasets def pass_functions(initial_tbl: pd.DataFrame, year: int, cobe: pd.DataFrame, bp: pd.DataFrame): return initial_tbl
None


**kwargs
dict
Keyword-arguments that will be passed to the function.
{}














Name
Type
Description





ArrowWrangler
ArrowWrangler instance with updated dataframe property.






>>> from pins.data import mtcars
>>> mtcars_arrow = pa.table(mtcars)
>>> c = ArrowWrangler(mtcars_arrow)
>>> mpg_wt = c.pipe_pandas(lambda d: d.loc[:, ['mpg', 'wt']])
>>> mpg_wt.dataframe.column_names
['mpg', 'wt']
>>> concat = mpg_wt.save_arrow_ifnew('mtcars_mpg_wt').pipe_pandas(
...     lambda d, mtcars_mpg_wt: pd.concat([d, mtcars_mpg_wt]), other_datasets=['mtcars_mpg_wt'])
>>> concat.dataframe.shape[0] == mtcars.shape[0] * 2
True




data_manipulation.ArrowWrangler.pipe_sql(
    sql_text,
    input_tbl_name='me',
    other_datasets=None,
)
Apply formula using sql via duckdb (tsql dialect).
Creates a view called ‘me’ to read sql from
Automatically convert form pyararow before function, and back to pyarrow after function.











Name
Type
Description
Default




sql_text
str
SQL script to run.
required


input_tbl_name
str
Name to get table alias eg so you can use SELECT * FROM me. Defaults to ‘me’.
'me'


other_datasets
list | None
List of strings defining the names of data pins to read from the board. This is used to create a duckdb view with that name to be able to query using sql.
None














Name
Type
Description





ArrowWrangler
ArrowWrangler instance with updated dataframe property.






>>> from pins.data import mtcars
>>> import pyarrow.compute as pc
>>> mtcars_arrow = pa.table(mtcars)
>>> c = ArrowWrangler(mtcars_arrow)
>>> cyl4 = c.pipe_sql('select * from me where cyl == 4')
>>> pc.max(cyl4.dataframe['cyl'])
<pyarrow.Int64Scalar: 4>
>>> union = cyl4.save_arrow_ifnew('car_cyl4').pipe_sql(
...  'select * from car_cyl4 union all select * from me', other_datasets=['car_cyl4'])
>>> union.dataframe.shape[0] == mtcars.query('cyl == 4').shape[0] * 2
True




data_manipulation.ArrowWrangler.read_from_board(board, name)
Read from board and save it to the object instance’s dataframe property.











Name
Type
Description
Default




board
pins.boards.BaseBoard
Pins board to read from.
required


name
str
Label for pin.
required














Name
Type
Description





ArrowWrangler | None
ArrowWrangler | None: ArrowWrangler instance with loaded dataframe, or None if pin not found.






>>> data = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2], 'b': [3, 4]})
>>> table = pa.Table.from_pandas(data)
>>> aw = ArrowWrangler(table)
>>> aw.board = pins.board_temp()
>>> _saved = aw.save_arrow_ifnew(name='simple')
>>> new = ArrowWrangler.read_from_board(aw.board, 'simple')
>>> new.dataframe.equals(pa.Table.from_pydict({'a': [1, 2], 'b': [3, 4]}))
True

title: data_tools
text:
data_tools
Module for data tools.





Name
Description




DataTools
Custom methods to add helper data and metadata.





data_tools.DataTools()
Custom methods to add helper data and metadata.





Name
Description




get_all_levels
Value Counts summary.


read_big_parquet
Read parquet file bigger than memory.


timing
Use as a decorator to print function name and time runs (s) and shape.





data_tools.DataTools.get_all_levels(data_con)
Value Counts summary.
For all the variables in the DataFrame, run value_counts with count and percentages and then stack them up into one DataFrame.





Name
Type
Description
Default




data_con
Table
Table with data to get levels from.
required














Name
Type
Description




Table
Table
Ibis Table with columns: level, count, percent, cum_perc, and column.






>>> from arrow_wrangler.data_tools import DataTools
>>> data = {"A": [1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2],
...        "B": ["a", "b", "a", "a", "b", "c"]}
>>> result = (DataTools.get_all_levels(ibis.memtable(data))
...     .mutate(percent=_['percent'].round(2)))
>>> result_df = pa.table({"level": ["1", "2", "a", "b", "c"],
...                          "count": [3, 3, 3, 2, 1],
...                          "variable": ["A", "A", "B", "B", "B"],
...                          "percent": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.33, 0.17]})
>>> result.to_pyarrow().equals(result_df)
True




data_tools.DataTools.read_big_parquet(parquet_location)
Read parquet file bigger than memory.
This is for larger than memory dataset. Uses arrows dataset object. Note this is different from the pyarrow table object (as used above as default) Uses in-memory, so is faster. Requires duckdb. This is a bit slower than the in_memory approach (ibis.read_parquet) but scales to larger-than-memory datasets!

required
